correctness.rationale: Let E_1,...,E_(d+1) be i.i.d. Exp(1), S=sum E_i, ε_i independent signs, X_i=ε_iE_i/S. Gamma–Dirichlet independence shows X has uniform normalized volume on B_1^d and S is independent of Y=sum_{i≤k}X_i. Since ε_iE_i are independent symmetric exponential/Laplace variables with characteristic function (1+t²)^(-1), SY has characteristic function (1+t²)^(-k) and even moments E[Y^(2n)]=(2n)!(k)_n/[n!(d+1)_(2n)]; odd moments vanish by sign symmetry. For W_k=I^(k-1)(1-r)^k, I f(r)=∫_r^1u f(u)du, repeated Fubini gives ∫_0^1r^m W_k(r)dr=B(m+2k-1,k+1)/prod_{j=0}^{k-2}(m+2j+1). Dividing m=2n by m=0 yields (2n)!(k)_n/[n!(3k)_(2n)]. At d=3k-1 every moment of two compactly supported symmetric probability laws agrees; polynomial density in C[-1,1] proves equality of measures and continuous density representatives p_k(y)=W_k(|y|)/(2∫W_k). For fixed k unit-weight coordinates and any d≥k, equality of second moments forces (d+1)(d+2)=3k(3k+1), strictly increasing and hence d=3k-1. Using d+1=3k exponentials and k independent signs yields the exact sampler. All statements hold for every integer k≥1, no multivariate/all-convex-bodies claim.
